Brand Origin
Origin
Brand Origin  ·  Origin
SnackLoop
The Snack Universe
Discover the endless possibilities of Asian snacks. SnackLoop is deeply rooted in Asian snack culture, curating specialty treats from Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia, and Taiwan — turning every bite into a small cultural adventure. We believe snacks are more than food; they're a bridge connecting memory and emotion.
Asian SnacksCurated ImportsLimited Editions
BaoPop
The Toy Universe
Welcome to the world of Bao characters, where the most authentic version of you lives. BaoPop centers on a round, plump bao bun IP, creating 6 designer toy characters that reflect the real emotions of today's youth — happy, chill, chaotic, working, overthinking, snacking... each one a mirror of your inner self.
Emotional Designer ToysBlind Box SeriesIP Collaboration
×
When Asian Snacks meet Emotional Designer Toys, SnackLoop × BaoPop is born — a third space where you can snack, unbox, and find resonance, all at once. Here, everyone can find today's version of themselves.
Brand Manifesto
Brand Manifesto
Brand Manifesto  ·  Brand Manifesto
Every mood
deserves a snack.
Every feeling deserves to be properly fed
Life is full of mood swings. Some days you're Happy Bao, charging into the world with a snack in hand. Some days you're Chill Bao, just wanting to lie down with boba. Some days you're Chaos Bao, with a thousand thoughts spiraling in your head.

We don't judge which Bao you are today. We're simply here — with the best snacks and the most comforting toys — to keep you company through every ordinary, real moment.
AuthenticityComfortSurpriseResonanceExclusivity

Logo Placement
Logo Placement  ·  Logo Placement
SnackLoop × BaoPop
① Top Left · Preferred Position
PREFERRED
SnackLoop × BaoPop
② Top Right · Alternate Position
SnackLoop × BaoPop
③ Centered · For Brand-Focused Scenarios
SnackLoop × BaoPop
④ Bottom Left · For Specific Scenarios
Placement Principles
When content is the focus → place the logo in a corner (top left preferred). When the brand is the focus → the logo can be centered and enlarged, while ensuring the clear space remains intact. The logo must never be cropped.

Secondary Color Usage Notes
Secondary colors are drawn directly from the signature palettes of the 6 BaoPop Friends characters, used for campaign materials, packaging series, and social media content where mood/series differentiation is needed. Each secondary color carries the emotional label of its corresponding character and should match that character's tone when used (e.g., Chaos Orange pairs with Chaos Bao's emotional-outburst theme).

Typography
Guidelines

Font System  ·  Brand Font System
Brand Typeface — English  ·  English Brand Typeface
Fredoka.
A soft, rounded geometric sans-serif typeface — its circular terminals and plump letterforms echo the round shape of BaoPop's bao bun characters, conveying a friendly, playful, and approachable brand personality. Suitable for headlines, logos, taglines, and all English-language applications.
Open-Source Font · Free for Commercial Use Google Fonts Rounded Geometric Style 5 Font Weights

Chinese Typeface
Brand Typeface — Chinese  ·  Chinese Brand Typeface
Can't Sit
Still Me
Recommended Fonts: Alibaba PuHuiTi / ZCOOL KuaiLe
Chinese text should use a rounded, modern sans-serif that matches Fredoka's tone. For headlines, a more characterful rounded font (such as ZCOOL KuaiLe) echoes BaoPop's playful energy, while body text uses PuHuiTi for clarity and readability. Both fonts are free for commercial use, avoiding copyright risk.
Headlines · ZCOOL KuaiLe Body · Alibaba PuHuiTi 3.0 Both Free for Commercial Use

IP Usage Guidelines
Usage Guidelines
🎨
Maintain the Color System
Each character has a dedicated color scheme that must not be arbitrarily altered. Character colors must be used strictly according to the guidelines to maintain recognizability.
📐
Proportions & Structure
BaoPop characters have a round, plump bao shape — a large head and small body are core features. Don't stretch, squash, or alter the head-to-body ratio; preserve the characters' cute, rounded feel.
✨
Emotional Consistency
Each character represents a specific emotion and should be matched to the appropriate context. Chaos Bao suits stress-related scenarios, while Happy Bao is for positive messaging.
✓  Correct Usage
Use official standard IP artwork
Keep each character's signature colors unchanged
Match the brand context and emotion
Can be paired with the brand logo
Can be scaled proportionally
✕  Prohibited Usage
Don't alter character colors or add filters
Don't stretch, distort, or rotate characters
Don't crop and isolate parts of a character
Don't pair with competitor brands
Don't add outline or shadow effects

Graphic
Element Library

Visual Element System  ·  Visual Element System
The SnackLoop × BaoPop visual system is built on 5 core graphic elements, used across stores, packaging, social media, and all communication touchpoints. Elements can be layered — more elements create a livelier, more festive look (great for campaigns), while fewer elements feel more restrained and minimal (great for everyday displays and business contexts).

5 Core Elements  ·  The 5 Core Elements

04
